edits.defect: Cross-contaminated attributions: al-Tabari credited with 'that I am His messenger to you' (not in his text — that content is al-Muyassar's), and al-Muyassar credited with a two-sided witness including 'your denial' (no takdhib clause in his text).
edits.before: Al-Tabari reads this as Allah commanding His Prophet to say to the idolaters: Allah is sufficient as a witness between me and you that I am His messenger to you, and He knows His servants. Ibn Kathir frames it similarly: Allah knows that the Prophet has conveyed what he was sent with, and He knows the condition of those addressed. Al-Muyassar states the heart of it: Allah is enough as a witness to my truthfulness and your denial; He is fully aware and seeing of His servants.
edits.after: Al-Tabari reads this as Allah commanding His Prophet to say it to the very people who had raised the objection — those who said to him, *has Allah sent a human being as a messenger?* Say to them: Allah is sufficient as witness between me and you, for He is the best Sufficient One and the Judge; He has knowledge of His servants' affairs and deeds, the one in the right among them and the one in the wrong, the guided and the astray. Ibn Kathir frames it similarly: Allah knows that the Prophet has conveyed what he was sent with, and He knows the condition of those addressed. Al-Muyassar states the heart of it: Allah is enough as witness to the Prophet's truthfulness and to the reality of his prophethood; He is aware of the states of His servants and seeing of their deeds, and will requite them for them.
edits.evidence: al-Tabari 17:96 (fetched): "يقول تعالى ذكره لنبيّه: قل يا محمد للقائلين لك ﴿أَبَعَثَ اللَّهُ بَشَرًا رَسُولا﴾ ﴿كَفَى بِاللَّهِ شَهِيدًا بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَكُمْ﴾ فإنه نعم الكافي والحاكم ﴿إِنَّهُ كَانَ بِعِبَادِهِ خَبِيرًا﴾ يقول: إن الله بعباده ذو خبرة وعلم بأمورهم وأفعالهم، والمحقّ منهم والمُبطل، والمُهدىّ والضالّ" — addressees identified by their objection; 'niʿma l-kāfī wa-l-ḥākim'; NO 'that I am His messenger to you'. al-Muyassar 17:96 (fetched, full text): "قل لهم: كفى بالله شهيدًا بيني وبينكم على صِدْقي وحقيقة نبوَّتي. إنه سبحانه خبير بأحوال عباده، بصير بأعمالهم، وسيجازيهم عليها." — ONE side only (ṣidqī wa-ḥaqīqati nubuwwatī); no denial/takdhīb clause anywhere.

edits.defect: Second assertion of the same false al-Muyassar attribution ('names both sides ... and their denial'), in Part 1 Element 3.
edits.before: Al-Muyassar explicitly names both sides: Allah is enough as witness to the Prophet's truthfulness and their denial. That double witness should make us careful.
edits.after: The wording itself is what names both sides. The Prophet is not told to say *shahidan li* — a witness *for* me — but `shahidan bayni wa-baynakum`, a witness *between* me and you. A witness placed between two parties is a witness over both of them, and al-Tabari's gloss on the second half moves in the same direction: Allah knows His servants' affairs, the one in the right among them and the one in the wrong. That double witness should make us careful.
edits.evidence: Re-grounded in the Qur'anic phrase per reviewer's named fix (the two-sided reading is a legitimate inference from بيني وبينكم, just not al-Muyassar's gloss). The supporting attribution added is al-Tabari's own verified wording: "ذو خبرة وعلم بأمورهم وأفعالهم، والمحقّ منهم والمُبطل" — the one in the right among them and the one in the wrong. al-Jalalayn 17:96 (fetched) likewise glosses شهيدا بيني وبينكم with "على صِدْقِي" only, confirming neither short edition carries the denial side.

edits.defect: Third assertion of the same false al-Muyassar attribution — and the load-bearing one, since Theme 2's central argument ('between means the whole space is exposed') rested on it.
edits.before: Al-Muyassar's reading is helpful because it makes both sides explicit: Allah witnesses the Prophet's truthfulness and the deniers' denial. In our conflicts, we often want Allah to witness one side only. But He is witness between me and you. Between means the whole space is exposed.
edits.after: The phrase itself is what makes both sides explicit. The witness is not requested *for* one party; He is placed *between* two. In our conflicts, we often want Allah to witness one side only. But He is witness between me and you. Between means the whole space is exposed.
edits.evidence: Same al-Muyassar text as above — one-sided. Theme 2 is preserved intact; only its ground shifts from an edition that does not carry it to the phrase بيني وبينكم, which the file has already parsed at Element 3. No sentence of the theme's argument was deleted.

edits.after: Al-Tabari reads the closing as Allah having knowledge of His servants' affairs and deeds, and seeing to their governance and disposal — nothing of their affairs hidden from Him. Not on the reviewer's named list, but the identical defect class, verified from the same fetch, and a four-word correction.

edits.defect: Ikhtilaf presented as consensus: chains-at-the-feet given as what 'the classical commentators' fill in, when al-Tabari adjudicates the qira'ah the other way (chains coordinated with the collars at the necks) and al-Jalalayn's FIRST option also puts them at the necks.
edits.before: The classical commentators fill in only what the verbs leave bare, and it is worth hearing. The collars — *al-aghlāl* — clamp at the neck; the chains — *al-salāsil* — bind at the feet; and the dragging is not metaphor but is done by hands, the *zabāniya*, the angels set over the punishment.
edits.after: The classical commentators fill in what the verbs leave bare, though not in one voice. The collars — *al-aghlāl* — clamp at the neck; the chains — *al-salāsil* — bind at the feet, on one reading: al-Muyassar says exactly that, and al-Jalālayn offers it as one option among several. But al-Jalālayn's first option coordinates the chains with the collars at the necks, and al-Ṭabarī settles the recitation the same way — the *rafʿ* reading, *al-salāsil* joined to *al-aghlāl* in *fī aʿnāqihim* — which he calls the correct reading, by the consensus of the authorities. On the dragging they agree: it is not metaphor but is done by hands, the *zabāniya*, the angels set over the punishment.
edits.evidence: al-Muyassar 40:70-72 (fetched): "حين تُجعل الأغلال في أعناقهم، والسلاسل في أرجلهم، وتسحبهم زبانية العذاب" — feet, plus zabaniya. al-Jalalayn 40:71 (fetched): "﴿والسَّلاسِل﴾ عُطِفَ عَلى الأَغْلال فَتَكُون فِي الأَعْناق أوْ مُبْتَدَأ خَبَره مَحْذُوف أيْ فِي أرْجُلهمْ أوْ خَبَره ﴿يُسْحَبُونَ﴾" — three options, the FIRST at the necks. al-Tabari 40:71 (fetched): "وقرأت قراءة الأمصار: والسلاسل، برفعها عطفا بها على الأغلال" and his ruling "والصواب من القراءة عندنا فى ذلك ما عليه قراء الأمصار، لإجماع الحجة عليه، وهو رفع السلاسل عطفا بها على ما في قوله: ﴿فِي أَعْنَاقِهِمْ﴾ من ذكر الأغلال" — chains at the necks, by ijmaʿ al-hujjah. al-Tabari also carries the zabaniya: "يسحب هؤلاء ... زبانية العذاب يوم القيامة في الحميم", so the dragging clause is genuinely agreed.

edits.after: These are two distinct nouns, not one noun at two stages of its life. al-Rāghib al-Iṣfahānī — a lexicographer rather than a commentator, so this is his *Mufradāt* and not one of the four tafsīr editions read alongside this passage — is explicit under this root: *al-ghull* is the specific name for the thing a person is bound with
